TS closes the window with two durable registry records (daemon-supervisor-ownership.ts at cd1f215): a startup fence (startup-fences/<sha256(socket)>.json pinning the dying predecessor's pid + process start id, persisted by the coordinator from the predecessor's verified hello, waited out at supervisor start - 10s default, 60s from the coordinator, 250ms poll, dead pins self-clear under the registry guard) and a shutdown admission (shutdown-admission.json, 5000ms lease renewed every 1000ms, acquired by the update coordinator and shutdown --all, refusing any ownership acquisition while active - code daemon_shutdown_in_progress). The rust tree had neither (the stop.rs module doc named the missing admission as a divergence; the supervisor's run() bound with no pre-bind gate). The candidate: port both arms 1:1 on the TS record shapes at ~/.prime/supervisor-owners (env PRIME_AGENT_INTERNAL_DAEMON_SUPERVISOR_REGISTRY_DIR), with the fence persisted by the real coordinator from the verified hello and the admission held across the whole stop, released immediately before the successor spawns.
